### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4a642058aa866bcdb62e3aef043dbd4e90a9e45` — the merge of head `045a193c3de6f617828245294cbbafd38c3048a4` into base `8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4a642058aa866bcdb62e3aef043dbd4e90a9e45 && git checkout d4a642058aa866bcdb62e3aef043dbd4e90a9e45
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1 045a193c3de6f617828245294cbbafd38c3048a4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1 && git merge --no-ff 045a193c3de6f617828245294cbbafd38c3048a4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**Requests to `GET /api/v1/meta/_drafts` now refused.** Any query name outside the closed set `package`, `type` is answered `400` with `error.code` `VALIDATION_ERROR` and the message `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` writes: `The "NAME" query parameter is not supported by this endpoint. ... Supported parameters: package, type.` That covers the retired `packageId`, a misspelt `typ`, a case variant `Package`, a bracketed spelling of a retired or unknown name (`packageId[]`), and an unknown name beside a known one (the unknown one is named; names are sorted). Before, every one of these was dropped: `?packageId=ID` answered the scoped list `200` and the rest answered the unscoped list `200`. On `RestServer` the body is the nested `{ error: { code, message } }` the list door writes; on the runtime dispatcher it is `deps.error(message, 400, { code })`, the dispatcher's `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }` envelope every dispatcher door already uses. `listDrafts` is never called for a refused request (pinned on both transports).

**Requests whose answer changes.** `?package=ID` reached `listDrafts` with no package before (the binding was not read) and answered every package's drafts `200`; it now reaches `listDrafts` as `{ packageId: 'ID' }` and answers that package's drafts. That is the card's defect, closed.

**`?package=ID`, `?package=all`, an unknown package, a draft-only package.** The value is read through `metaItemPackageBinding` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`): a non-empty string other than `all` is the package; `all`, the empty value and a non-string name no package. So `?package=all` and an absent `package` both list every package (`listDrafts` receives `packageId: undefined`; pinned on both transports). A package that is neither installed nor bound to a pending draft is refused by `listDrafts` itself (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-drafts.ts`): `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, "'ID' is not an installed package, and no pending draft is bound to it..." — unchanged by this PR and pinned as a CONTROL on the REST route. A package bound only to a pending draft passes that rule ("a draft bound to the package is proof enough") and answers `200` with its drafts; with a `?type=` it has no draft of, the second `listDrafts` read finds the binding and the answer is the honest empty list. The protocol's own refusal text still says "omit packageId to list every package's drafts": that names the protocol request field, not the wire key, so it stays true.

**`?packageId=` retired.** Refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `packageId`; no alias, no deprecation window. `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.drafts` and the `META_BRACKETED_FILTERS.drafts` entry are respelled to `package`, so a repeated or bracketed `packageId` is now the recognition step's unknown name, not the arity step's. The test that said "`_drafts` reads no `package`" is respelled accordingly.

**`?type=`.** Unchanged in reading: one metadata type, an unknown type refused by `refuseUnknownMetaListType` (the list door's verdict), the empty value every type. New: a misspelt `typ` is `400`, and `type[]` keeps its located bracketed refusal.

**Bracketed keys.** `package[]`, `package[0]`, `package[id]`, `type[]`, `type[0]`, `type[name]` are refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` by `metaBracketedFilterRefusal` with the respelled sentence ("the 'package' filter takes exactly one package id, spelled ?package=ID ..."); recognition leaves exactly the keys opening `package[` and `type[` to that sentence. `packageId[]` and `packages[]` are unknown names. A repeated plain `package` beside a bracketed `type` answers the multiplicity sentence first.

**No params.** `200` with every package and every type (`listDrafts({ packageId: undefined, type: undefined })`), pinned as CONTROL on both transports.

**REST server and runtime dispatcher answering identically.** Both ask the same three decisions in the same order after the same two gates: the authoring-capability gate (403 first, so an unauthorised caller cannot probe the query rules), the `listDrafts` capability probe (501), then recognition (`metaDraftsUnknownParamRefusal`), arity (`refuseRepeatedQueryParams` on REST, `repeatedOnceRefusal` inside `metaQueryArityRefusal` on the dispatcher, same list), then the bracketed refusal; both then `refuseUnknownMetaListType` and `metaItemPackageBinding(query.package)`. The dispatcher's `metaDraftsQueryRefusal` is literally recognition `??` `metaQueryArityRefusal('drafts')`. Status and `error.code` agree; the envelopes differ only as they already differ for every dispatcher door (and the 403 code, `FORBIDDEN` on REST and `PERMISSION_DENIED` on the dispatcher, is pre-existing and untouched). The parity pins compare each transport's `_drafts` refusal to its own list door's.

**The two new root exports.** `packages/rest/src/index.ts` adds `META_DRAFTS_QUERY_PARAMS` (a frozen `['package', 'type']`) and `metaDraftsQueryRefusal`; the dispatcher imports the latter from `@objectstack/rest`. `metaDraftsUnknownParamRefusal` stays internal, reached by the REST route through the `metaReadGate` namespace, which mirrors how `metaListUnknownParamRefusal` is kept internal beside the exported `META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS` and `metaListQueryRefusal`. Neither export changes an existing one.

**Client and data-objectstack.** `ObjectStackClient.meta.listDrafts({ packageId, type })` and `MetadataClient.listDrafts({ packageId, type })` keep both option names and set `package` on the wire (`URLSearchParams.set('package', ...)` and `package=${encodeURIComponent(...)}`); `type` is unchanged. Both docblocks say the wire spelling moved. Pinned by the client test (`?package=com.acme.crm&type=object`) and the two data-objectstack tests. The Console's four hand-built URLs (`usePendingDrafts.draftsUrl`, three in `PackagesPage.PackageDetailSheet`) are respelled, and every other app-shell reader (`AutomationsFlowRail`, `ObjectHooksPanel`, `ObjectListViewInspector`, `PackageOwdOverviewPanel`, five sites in `StudioDesignSurface`) goes through `MetadataClient.listDrafts` with the unchanged option name. The ui test fakes that read `searchParams.get('packageId')` are respelled to `package`, so the fakes model the new door.

### ② Semver level

**All four packages `patch`.** Correct under maintainer ruling A on #25105 (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3): the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone; `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/client` and `@object-ui/data-objectstack` are the four published packages the diff moves; `@object-ui/app-shell` is private and `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` changes a jsdoc only. `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base`) is complete and green on this head.

**The `!` and the BREAKING banner.** The title `fix(rest)!:`, the changeset's first line (`fix(rest)!:`) and its `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing` section agree with the code: a query answered `200` before is now `400`, and a wire key is retired. The banner on a `patch` is the sanctioned shape.

**`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with a widening half.** Read from the diff: the accept set narrows (unknown names and `packageId` refused) and the public face widens by two `@objectstack/rest` exports. `no (widening)` is malformed and `no (narrowing)` would deny the exports, so `yes (narrowing)` is the only true spelling; it is the shape the #23214 precedent in `packages/rest/CHANGELOG.md` used for exactly this pattern (arity narrowing plus new rest exports). The seat's second amendment, from `no (narrowing)` to `yes (narrowing)`, is therefore right, and the PR body, changeset and amendment all carry the same line.

**`Metadata-protocol: none`.** Correct: nothing a metadata author writes changes — no spec key, value, type or default. The `listDrafts` request type is unchanged (`request?: { packageId?: string; type?: string }` on `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation#listDrafts` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` and `protocol-drafts.ts`), and only `ListDraftsResponseSchema` lives in `packages/spec`. The claim's substance holds; its name does not. Nit (F2).

**The ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition.** Judged consistent. Nothing `objectstack migrate meta` can reach moves: no spec key, authorable spelling, stored row or exported declaration is removed or re-shaped, and the two new exports are additions. The body's `**The remedy.** FROM ... TO ...` line is the same shape the three earlier narrowings of this door and its siblings carried under the same disposition (the #29440 `_drafts` bracketed-key changeset, the list and book-tree `package[]` changeset and the app `id[]` changeset, all in `packages/rest/CHANGELOG.md`), and `findMigrationPrescription` reads FROM/TO only as a positioned label or beside an arrow rewrite, so the gate passed on this head for the same reason it passed those. ADR-0087's D-table does say a FROM/TO block refuses this category, for a type-surface change; on a REST query spelling the house precedent is the four changesets above, and this one follows them. No finding.

**The FROM/TO remedy.** Present and correct: FROM `GET /api/v1/meta/_drafts?packageId=ID` TO `GET /api/v1/meta/_drafts?package=ID`, plus "upgrade `@objectstack/client` and `@object-ui/data-objectstack` together with the server". It does not say what happens when they are not upgraded together in the new-client direction (see ③, F1).

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev `open_questions[0]` — callers outside this repository (cloud) unmeasured.** This review cannot measure cloud either; it is outside the inputs. What is measured: every in-repo wire sender of `?packageId=` is migrated (a grep of the PR tree finds the old spelling only in `CHANGELOG.md` files, the release-owned `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`, the history table in `dispatcher-query-arity.test.ts` and one source comment, F3), `packages/mcp` has no `_drafts` caller, and hotcrm at 6961ab13 has none. The retirement itself holds without the cloud measurement: Prime Directive 12 forbids a lenient alias in the REST layer and admits a tolerated alias only as a declared ADR-0087 conversion entry, which nobody has claimed for an unnamed external caller; rule 5's closed set is measured from the read points, not from possible callers. Escalated to the seat as the dev proposed: option A (the cloud lane runs the dedupe search `_drafts packageId` and `listDrafts packageId` before the release reaches cloud) is the right one, and option B's fallback is loud (a `400` naming `packageId` and listing `package`, `type`), not silent. Not a FAIL.

**The seat's "startup rule" (an alias spelling retires immediately unless a named external user needs it).** Not located in AGENTS.md, docs/agents or docs/adr. The repository rules that carry the same decision are Prime Directive 12 and rule 5; the record relies on those.

**The seat's file-surface amendment.** The PR's 51 files sit inside the amended surface (REST route, runtime twin, shared read gate, `@objectstack/client`, `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, `usePendingDrafts.ts`, `PackagesPage.tsx`, the dogfood tests, the QA checklist, tests, the changeset). Three touches are outside the named list and are prose- or label-only: `packages/rest/src/index.ts` (the two exports, announced in the Clause-② amendment), `packages/objectql/src/package-disable-enforcement.test.ts` (a reader label), `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` (a jsdoc). Acceptable.

No concern.

The source comment in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts` ("`_drafts?packageId=` does not") now names a retired wire key as if current. Nit (F3).

**Version skew.** (a) Old client against new server: an `@objectstack/client` or `@object-ui/data-objectstack` at or below 18.3.0, or an old `@objectstack/console` bundle, sends `?packageId=` and gets `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming it; the Studio pending-drafts bar and the package detail sheet would surface an error, not a wrong list. Loud, and the changeset names the fix. `@objectstack/console` is consumed by `packages/cli` at `workspace:*`, so it ships lock-step with the server, and `packages/console/dist` is not committed, so no stale bundle sits in the tree. ### ④ Design judgment

**A caller outside the repo still sending `packageId`.** Gets a located `400` whose message names `packageId` and lists `package`, `type`; `listDrafts` is never called. The remedy is one word on the wire, or an SDK upgrade with no code change.
